questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I could have courses taught in both english and spanish as well as a general interest in the culture of Mexico and Latin America.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a trip to the city of Puebla, and other practical information during the first days before the semester started.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was quite easy as one of my friends had studied at UDLAP one year before me, and she recommended me a place to stay. The place i lived is called Casa Leyenda, and it was really a good place, for me it had the perfect combination of social vibes and private space. So definetely a big recommendation, i made most of my friendships with people in the house i lived in.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That you will have more freedom than if you live on campus. For me it worked well that uni was a place to study and when i left uni i had more of a feeling of free time when coming home.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was really difficult to register courses, as they had to match courses that i would otherwise have had on my own campus, so they had to be accepted by my own uni. On the website on UDLAP there's no syllabuses and not a lot of information about the courses, so it took a while to get everything accepted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have an international office that you can send e-mails to for help and questions. The reply time was quite long sometimes though.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the 4/5 of the courses i applied for. then i had to change 1.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start in good time so you dont get stressed with everything in the end. The preparation for going on an exchange is a long process with many practical things to get in order before.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think that the level of the courses was as expected.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was in general the same style of teaching, with a lot of interaction and inclusion of the students in the classroom.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LIO3022 - Pragmatica
LPT2042 Sistemas politicos comparados
LRI2022- History of International Relations
LRI3052 - CONTEMPORARY LATIN AMERICA
LRP2032 - Comunicacion y Globalizacion

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My favorite two courses were sistemas politicos comparados and history of international relations. They are both available in english and international relations also in spanish. I really liked them because of the topic.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are sports clubs and a nice gym. Honestly i didn't really use any of the social activites at the uni.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fiestaaa

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel! It's a beautiful country with amazing people and culture.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Of course it's always a bit of a culture shock arriving to a place so different than what you're used to at home. But for me i quickly got used to it and grew to like it more and more.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people that you have classes with. Everyone at uni speaks good english, but if you can speak a bit of spanish it's an amazing way to connect to people as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people, the food, the music

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find a nice place to live, i would definetly recommend staying outside of campus, but of course everyone is different. Learn just a bit of spanish before, it will make your life there much easier and more fun. The bureacracy in Mexico is slow, even in universities, so start your paperwork early.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships and people that i met, and the cultural insight i got. It's different living in a country for 5 months than just travelling, you really get a different feeling of how people are and live.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having 4 final exams in 4 days..

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
